text: 🚨 We're hiring! 🚨 Looking for a product designer to join our team in Lisbon. Hybrid, 3 days in the office. ♻️ Repost to help me reach the right person!

We looked at 3 years of support tickets to understand churn. The surprise: customers who filed one ticket churned less than those who filed none, because silent customers never told us what was wrong. However, after the third ticket churn doubled. Therefore we now call every customer after their second ticket. In the first quarter this cut churn from 4.1% to 3.2% per month, measured against a holdout group of 2,000 accounts. The lesson for us was that tickets are a signal of engagement until they are a signal of frustration, and the turning point is measurable.

Why our p99 latency dropped from 900 ms to 140 ms: the database was fine, the connection pool was not. Every request opened a TLS connection because the pool was sized below our concurrency. We measured with a load test at 2,000 requests per second, raised the pool from 20 to 120, and pinned connections per worker. In contrast to what we expected, CPU use went down because the handshakes were the expensive part. The benchmark scripts are in our engineering blog post.
